 Our Rain Free Pattern Gets Extended 
 Mornings stay chilly with mild 70 degree afternoons 
 Mornings stay chilly with mild 70 degree afternoons By Brad Maushart Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 9:39 AM EDT | Updated : Oct. 21, 2026 at 7:08 PM EDT Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CINCINNATI (WXIX) - One of the driest stretches of 2026 continues across the Tri-State, and there’s little sign of that changing anytime soon. Comfortable temperatures, plenty of sunshine and chilly mornings will carry us through the weekend and much of next week. Our next meaningful opportunity for rain may not arrive until just before Halloween.
 Thursday and Friday offer more of the same, with highs in the upper 60s and plenty of sunshine. A few high, thin clouds may filter the sun at times, but there’s no rain in sight. Morning fog could remain pesky in some communities, especially north of Cincinnati. Otherwise, it’s a great stretch of weather for getting outside, catching up on yardwork or enjoying the fall colors. Just remember to dress in layers for those chilly mornings.
 The weekend looks equally inviting. Saturday brings sunshine and a high near 68, while Sunday turns a little milder with temperatures climbing into the lower 70s. Whether you’re headed to a football game, visiting a pumpkin patch or tackling some Halloween decorating, the weather should cooperate. Both days remain dry with relatively light winds.
 Our dry streak continues into the beginning of next week. Monday could reach 73 degrees before temperatures settle closer to 70 Tuesday and Wednesday. Clouds will gradually become more common, but rain chances remain very low. In fact, we may go nearly two weeks without measurable rainfall in many communities before our next weather system arrives.
 That next opportunity for rain appears to be Thursday night into Friday, Oct. 30. A cold front could bring scattered showers, thunderstorms and gusty winds, prompting a First Alert Weather Day for Friday. There’s still plenty of uncertainty this far out, especially with the timing and strength of the system. For now, the latest forecast suggests most rain could exit by early Friday afternoon.
 The good news for Halloween plans is that the forecast currently favors drier and cooler weather by Saturday, Oct. 31. Highs should reach the mid 60s with at least some sunshine, and temperatures could settle into the 50s during trick-or-treat hours. We’ll continue fine-tuning that forecast as Halloween gets closer.
